documents.name: Major Project Synopsis.pdf
documents.summary: This document is a major project synopsis for 'EduVerse,' an interactive learning platform developed in Unreal Engine 5 by students at the Jaypee Institute of Information Technology. The proposed platform aims to enhance student engagement by generating personalized MetaHuman digital twins from facial scans to act as playable avatars. It integrates a custom ESP32 motion controller and LLM-powered non-player characters to guide students through an educational escape room challenge. Ultimately, the system provides an active, immersive learning environment with embedded assessment across multiple technical subjects.

PROBLEM STATEMENT  
 
Most engineering courses still run on lectures, textbooks, slides and online quizzes. These deliver 
theory efficiently and leave the student as a passive receiver. Concepts that are spatial or procedural 
suffer the most from this. It is hard to build real intuition for how a circuit responds to a fault or 
how a sorting algorithm moves through memory by reading a static diagram and when engagement 
drops, retention drops

a circuit responds to a fault or 
how a sorting algorithm moves through memory by reading a static diagram and when engagement 
drops, retention drops with it. 
Real-time game engines have already solved the visualisation half of that problem for other 
industries. Unreal Engine 5 handles lighting, physics and rendering at interactive frame rates[1] 
and Epic’s MetaHuman framework produces digital humans with production-quality facial rigs. 
Almost all of that capability currently points at games, film and virtual production[9]. Educational 
software has barely touched it. 
Avatars are a specific symptom. Virtual learning environments that include characters usually hand 
the student a fixed set of stock models or stylised figures. The student picks something that is not 
them and then watches

e characters usually hand 
the student a fixed set of stock models or stylised figures. The student picks something that is not 
them and then watches it move around the world. A character built from the student’s own face 
changes that relationship and the pipeline to produce one now exists outside research labs. 
Interaction is the second gap. Movement in these environments runs through a keyboard, mouse 
or standard gamepad, none of which were designed for embodied presence. Conversation with in-
world characters is usually a dialogue tree authored in advance, so a character can only answer 
questions the developer anticipated. A student stuck on something the script did not cover gets 
nothing useful back.

This project proposes MirrorVerse, a digital twin learning platform built in Unreal Engine 5. A 
user scans their face with a phone camera, the scan is converted into a MetaHuman through the 
Mesh to MetaHuman pipeline and the result becomes a fully playable character. Navigation and 
object interaction run through a custom ESP32 controller built around an inertial sensor and 
joystick. Speech is captured, classified for emotional content and mapped onto the MetaHuman 
facial rig, so the twin reacts while the user talks. Non-player characters are backed by a language 
model rather than a dialogue tree, which lets them handle questions nobody wrote down in 
advance. 
 
 
 
 
 

 
The learning content sits inside an educational

The learning content sits inside an educational escape challenge. The player starts in a virtual 
facility on a countdown. Every room is locked and each door opens only after a subject problem 
is solved. The problems cover programming, electronics, mathematics, artificial intelligence and 
logical reasoning and they get harder the deeper the player goes. 
 
What the system offers: 
• A learning environment where the student plays as themselves instead of a stock avatar, 
which raises the stake they have in the session. 
• Interaction through voice, facial expression and a purpose-built motion controller rather 
than a keyboard and mouse. 
• NPC tutors that answer unscripted questions and

h voice, facial expression and a purpose-built motion controller rather 
than a keyboard and mouse. 
• NPC tutors that answer unscripted questions and adapt their explanations to where the 
player is stuck. 
• Assessment that is built into gameplay, so progress through the facility is itself a record of 
what the student solved and how long it took. 
• A platform structure that can be re-skinned for other subjects and beyond that for healthcare 
training, corporate onboarding or remote classrooms. 
  
                                                 
  
    
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
  OBJECTIVES   
  
1. Build a digital twin learning platform in Unreal Engine 5 in which a scanned human face 
becomes a fully playable MetaHuman character. 
2. Implement the face scanning and MetaHuman generation

becomes a fully playable MetaHuman character. 
2. Implement the face scanning and MetaHuman generation pipeline, converting phone-
camera facial data into a rigged 3D character that preserves likeness and support multiple 
user profiles through the same pipeline. 
3. Develop  a  character  management  system  that  stores  user  details,  MetaHuman  assets, 
customisation settings, gameplay progress and achievements, so a twin can be reloaded 
across sessions. 
4. Build a custom ESP32 motion controller combining an inertial measurement unit, joystick 
and wireless link and integrate it as an input device inside Unreal Engine. 
5. Implement voice-driven facial expression: capture speech, classify its emotional content 
and drive the MetaHuman facial

and drive the MetaHuman facial rig to show happiness, sadness, anger, surprise or a neutral 
state. 
6. Design the educational escape challenge, where puzzles in programming, electronics, 
mathematics, artificial intelligence and logical reasoning unlock doors across multiple 
timed levels of increasing difficulty. 
7. Integrate AI-driven NPCs that give contextual hints, explain concepts and hold open-ended 
conversation with the player rather than reading from a fixed dialogue tree. 
8. Add multiplayer support so several scanned users can occupy one environment and either 
collaborate on or compete over the same challenges. 
9. Evaluate the finished system on likeness accuracy,

9. Evaluate the finished system on likeness accuracy, controller latency, speech recognition

INTRODUCTION  
  
A digital twin is a virtual model kept in correspondence with something real. The idea started in 
industry, where twins of turbines, factory lines and supply chains are used for simulation and 
monitoring and it has since spread into healthcare and urban planning. Applying it to a person 
rather than a machine is newer ground[7]. A twin of a learner is not a sensor-fed model of a 
physical asset but a visual and behavioural stand-in that the learner controls and the value of it 
comes from

learner is not a sensor-fed model of a 
physical asset but a visual and behavioural stand-in that the learner controls and the value of it 
comes from identification rather than prediction. 
Two pieces of technology make this practical now. Unreal Engine 5 gives real-time rendering, 
physics and lighting good enough that a virtual space reads as a place rather than a diagram[8]. 
MetaHuman  gives  a  face  rig  detailed  enough  to  carry  expression,  along  with  the  Mesh  to 
MetaHuman workflow, which takes a scanned facial mesh and fits a full production character to 
it. Together they let an ordinary phone scan become a character with a working face in a matter of 
hours instead of a modelling contract. 
MirrorVerse uses both to build a learning platform around the student’s own likeness.

MirrorVerse uses both to build a learning platform around the student’s own likeness. The system 
has four parts. 
 
Personalised digital twin 
The user’s face is scanned on a phone and converted to a MetaHuman through the Mesh to 
MetaHuman workflow. The generated character is imported into Unreal Engine and set up as a 
playable third-person character with full body animation. A character management layer keeps 
multiple user profiles, each holding its MetaHuman asset, customisation choices, progress and 
achievements, so a returning user loads their own twin and picks up where they left off. 
 
Natural interaction 
Movement and object interaction run on a custom ESP32 controller[10]. Tilt and rotation from an 
inertial sensor

hey left off. 
 
Natural interaction 
Movement and object interaction run on a custom ESP32 controller[10]. Tilt and rotation from an 
inertial sensor drive camera and character movement, a joystick handles fine positioning and the 
whole thing talks to the engine wirelessly. Alongside it, a speech pipeline listens to the user, 
identifies commands and emotional tone and triggers the matching expression on the MetaHuman 
face. Saying something in frustration and watching the twin’s face register it closes the loop 
between the user and the character in a way a keypress does not. 
 

 
Educational escape challenge 
The main gameplay is a timed escape from a virtual facility. Each room is sealed and each door is 
tied to a problem drawn from programming, electronics, mathematics, artificial intelligence

a virtual facility. Each room is sealed and each door is 
tied to a problem drawn from programming, electronics, mathematics, artificial intelligence or 
logical reasoning. Solve it and the door opens. The countdown supplies pressure, the difficulty 
curve supplies progression and the puzzle set is where the actual subject content lives. 
 
AI-assisted learning 
NPCs placed through the facility act as tutors. They are driven by a language model[3], so a player 
can ask them to explain a concept, request a hint on the current door or ask a follow-up question 
that goes off-script and get a coherent answer. This is what separates the platform from a quiz app 
with better graphics. 
Bringing digital twins, MetaHuman, embedded hardware, speech processing and language models 
into a single application

uiz app 
with better graphics. 
Bringing digital twins, MetaHuman, embedded hardware, speech processing and language models 
into a single application is the technical contribution here. The educational contribution is showing 
whether a student who plays as themselves, talks to their tutors and solves problems under a clock 
learns more than one working through the same material on a slide deck. 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
                                             METHODOLOGY  
 
The work splits into five stages covering twin generation, data management, gameplay, hardware 
and AI integration and evaluation. 
 
1. Digital twin creation 
Facial data is captured with a smartphone camera and processed into a mesh. The mesh is passed 
through the Mesh to MetaHuman workflow to produce a rigged

al data is captured with a smartphone camera and processed into a mesh. The mesh is passed 
through the Mesh to MetaHuman workflow to produce a rigged MetaHuman, which is then 
imported into Unreal Engine 5 and configured as a playable third-person character with a full 
animation blueprint. Each generated character is tied to a unique player profile and stored for reuse. 
Scan quality, lighting and capture angle all affect the final likeness, so this stage includes testing 
the capture procedure to find a repeatable setup. 
 
2. Character management system 
A local database, built on SQLite[11], holds everything that needs to persist between sessions: 
• Player profiles and login details 
• MetaHuman asset references 
• Character customisation settings 
• Level progress and puzzle state

Unreal’s save game system writes to this layer, so a user can quit mid-run and reload into the same 
room with the same twin. 
 
3. Educational escape challenge 
Levels are built as a sequence of sealed rooms with a global countdown. Each door is bound to a 
puzzle drawn from one of five subject pools: programming, electronics, mathematics, artificial 
intelligence and logical reasoning. Puzzles are authored as data assets so the set can be extended 
without touching level logic. Difficulty scales as the player moves through the facility and puzzle 
state is written back to the database on each solve.

state is written back to the database on each solve. 
 

 
4. AI interaction and controller                      
The  ESP32  controller  is  built  around  an  inertial  measurement  unit  and  analogue  joystick, 
programmed through ESP-IDF and connected to the engine over a wireless link. Motion is mapped 
to character movement and camera control, with joystick input for precise positioning and buttons 
for interaction. 
On the software side, speech from the microphone is transcribed and classified for emotional 
content[4] and the result is mapped onto the MetaHuman facial rig through blend shapes. NPC 
dialogue is handled by a language model reached through an API[12], with the current room,

ed onto the MetaHuman facial rig through blend shapes. NPC 
dialogue is handled by a language model reached through an API[12], with the current room, 
puzzle and player history passed in as context so hints are relevant to where the player actually is. 
 
5. Integration, testing and evaluation 
All modules are brought together into one build and tested on: 
• Likeness accuracy of the generated MetaHuman against the source scan 
• Controller latency and motion tracking stability 
• Speech recognition and emotion classification accuracy 
• Puzzle logic, door unlocking and timer behaviour 
• NPC response relevance and response time 
• Frame rate and overall usability 
Evaluation is run with a group of student users, comparing task completion, retention on the puzzle 
subjects and self-reported

and overall usability 
Evaluation is run with a group of student users, comparing task completion, retention on the puzzle 
subjects and self-reported immersion against a conventional presentation of the same material.
